chapter_title: Concerning the Five Saviours, the Resurrectors of
spiritual_reading:
This chapter cannot be coherently translated in full because most of its content is missing; the surviving phrases do not provide enough function or context to determine the spiritual sense of the elided subjects and actions.

Within what remains, a sequence of Divine operations is being named as successive means of restoration.

A second operation of restoration is mentioned, but its nature is unclear because the defining content has been removed.

A third operation of restoration is attributed to the Divine Itself as the primal source, because by Divine truth all living goods and truths are collected out of dispersion, turned back into order under the Divine, and then receive what is proper to their renewed state and enter a state of peace.

A fourth operation of restoration is attributed to enlightened understanding, because illumination in the intellect effects renewal; the specific mechanism here is uncertain because the explanatory clause is missing.

A fifth operation of restoration, directed toward those in good, is attributed again to the Divine Itself as the One first in order and permanence. This operation holds all subordinate faculties in unity and stability, removes what has been concealing and restraining their right action, and draws them inward toward conjunction with the Divine according to Divine love. By that conjunction they are re-formed, lifted out of lower disorder into a standing state in true order, and preserved there until the appointed completion of the process.

fills.fill: the lives are planted in their forms
fills.notes: The surviving “… i]t therein …” implies an impersonal placement or implantation. In the oldest substrate register, restoration begins with lives being set within their proper vessels or forms (inside → outside).

In the Iranian-Manichaean cosmological sequence, the Living Spirit functions as an early restoring power after the first saving summons, effecting extraction and re-ordering of the mixed lives. With the defining clause lost, the safest substrate-consistent title for a ‘second resurrector’ is the Living Spirit.

The line already reads “the Father, the First […]”; the substrate title paired with ‘First’ here is the primal stability or permanence of the Divine. “Established One” keeps the impersonal cosmological register and matches ¶6’s repeated epithet.
Correspondentially required: the Divine Word gathers lives out of dispersion. This supplies the needed opposite of ‘gather in and go to him’.
After regathering, lives ‘receive’ what is proper to their renewed state and then ‘rest’. In the substrate this is expressed as receiving their proper form or measure (order in ultimates).

fills.fill: he enlightens the lives and turns them toward their likeness
fills.notes: The Light Mind restores by illumination in the intellect: giving light to understanding and turning what is being restored toward its archetypal pattern. This matches the chapter’s stated mechanism for the fourth operation.
The phrase “to the good […]” in this register most naturally takes ‘lives’ as the subject-class being restored (good lives as recipients).
The Father is repeated as “First established one”; the clause after it should state the mode: acting from steadfast permanence (stability as the ground of re-ordering).
The following clause is “[He ...] all the powers,” which correspondentially demands an action of holding-together in unity; “binds” is the substrate verb for unification under a higher principle.

fills.fill: in the root of his stability
fills.notes: “and he stands firm […]” calls for a ground or basis. In correspondences, firmness is from first principles (root), not from outward constraint.
“He shall unveil the […] over them” requires the object removed: a covering that conceals and restrains. The most economical noun is ‘veil’.
The veil is typically described as laid or spread over. This supplies a natural action consistent with the image and keeps the impersonal tone.

fills.fill: by the attraction of his light
fills.notes: “and he draws them to him […]” needs an instrument or means; in this substrate the drawing is by light (intellectual-spiritual attraction), not by moral exhortation.
After drawing, “his will […]” should state what the will functions as for them: their rule, measure, or order. ‘Measure’ fits correspondentially (order determining form).
“and he […] them” in this context is the act of re-forming into stability after conjunction: establishing them in ordered state.
“and he stands them up […] there” calls for their ordered placement. ‘Rank’ expresses discrete degrees and ordered function.
They remain until an appointed end-state. In the oldest layer this is not judgment-language but process-language: the completion/consummation of the restoration.

assessment: Most restorations are constrained by the chapter’s clear sequence of successive restoring operations and by the repeated epithet ‘First established one’. However, ¶2 and the explanatory clauses for the second and fourth resurrectors are genuinely underdetermined in the surviving natural text; those fills are therefore guided primarily by the correspondential requirements (implantation into forms; restoration by illumination) and remain tentative to moderate in exact wording.
